title: HfO2/SiO2 20-layer emissivity selective stack on Si with gradient thickness optimization
scientific_hypothesis: A 20-layer alternating HfO2/SiO2 stack with individually optimized thicknesses can achieve higher emissivity in 8-13 μm than in 3-5 μm on a Si substrate, with the contrast arising from destructive interference in the target band and constructive interference in the suppressed band.
design_principle: Recalled knowledge: By Kirchhoff's law, emissivity equals absorptance at thermal equilibrium. For an opaque Si substrate in IR, emissivity = 1 - reflectance. A dielectric mirror stack creates high reflectance at wavelengths where layer optical thicknesses are quarter-wave multiples. By deviating from quarter-wave thicknesses, reflectance can be suppressed in the 8-13 μm band while maintained in 3-5 μm. HfO2 has higher refractive index than SiO2, providing the index contrast needed for interference effects.
proposed_topology: air | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | HfO2 | SiO2 | si substrate (20 dielectric layers total, alternating starting with HfO2)
design_variables: individual layer thicknesses for all 20 layers, each tunable independently within 200-3000 nm bounds
soft_objectives: maximize mean emissivity in 8000-13000 nm band
minimize mean emissivity in 3000-5000 nm band
maintain physically valid candidates (no negative thickness, no absorption violations)
manufacturing_considerations: total layer count fixed at 20 (within 24-layer limit)
individual layer thicknesses should remain within depositable range (200-3000 nm)
theory_basis: Recalled: Kirchhoff's law states emissivity equals absorptance for bodies in thermal equilibrium
Recalled: For opaque substrate, emissivity = 1 - reflectance (transmittance negligible)
Recalled: Quarter-wave stacks produce high reflectance bands; deviating from quarter-wave suppresses reflectance
Recalled: HfO2 refractive index is higher than SiO2 in IR range, providing index contrast for interference
Recalled: Si is opaque in mid-IR due to free carrier absorption and phonon absorption
Recalled: Gradient thickness optimization can find non-intuitive layer sequences that outperform periodic designs
expected_advantages: 20 layers provides sufficient degrees of freedom for spectral shaping
Alternating high/low index materials maximize interference contrast
Individual thickness tuning allows band-specific optimization rather than periodic constraint
Si substrate provides opaque backing so emissivity tracking is straightforward
known_risks: I am uncertain about exact n/k values for HfO2 and SiO2 in 3-13 μm range - these must come from the material catalog datasets, not my memory
I am uncertain whether HfO2 or SiO2 have intrinsic absorption peaks in the target bands that would affect design - this would be revealed by the catalog data
I am uncertain about typical thickness deposition tolerances for these oxides in thermal evaporation - assuming 200-3000 nm is depositable but this should be verified
I am uncertain whether 20 layers is optimal versus 22 or 24 - this route tests 20 specifically, but other layer counts might perform better
The prior iterations showed some physics_violation and solver_disagreement failures - this suggests numerical sensitivity that the relaxed penalty should address
execution_request_english: Optimize a 20-layer planar dielectric stack on silicon substrate with air incidence. Layer sequence: HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat), HfO2, SiO2 (Kischkat) (alternating, starting with HfO2, ending with SiO2 (Kischkat) before substrate). All 20 layer thicknesses are independent optimization variables with bounds 200-3000 nm. Wavelength bands: 3000-5000 nm (suppress emissivity) and 8000-13000 nm (maximize emissivity). Polarization: unpolarized or both TE and TM averaged. Incidence angle: 0 degrees (normal). Objective: maximize emissivity contrast between the two bands using gradient thickness optimization with quadratic penalty weight 0.02 and perturbation bound ±0.2%. Material names must resolve to hfo2, SiO2 (Kischkat), and si from the catalog. Report best_target_score, valid_candidates count, tightest_margin, and thicknesses_nm for all candidates.
revision_reason: Continuation route following feedback directives: relaxed quadratic penalty weight from 0.025 to 0.02 and expanded perturbation bound from ±0.15% to ±0.2% to widen searchable parameter space and recover valid candidate diversity while leveraging high margin safety buffer
